10-notes/concepts/conditional-access.title: Conditional Access
10-notes/concepts/conditional-access.html:
Conditional Access

Idea: access decisions are policy-driven 'if-then' rules over signals such as user, device, location and app, rather than a static allow or deny.

  • Delivered by: microsoft-entra-id P1, so it is included in ems-e3 and microsoft-365-e3.
  • Pairs with: MFA (a common control) and device compliance from microsoft-intune.

Now sourced: the signals are (user/group membership, IP location, device state, application) and the decisions (allow, require MFA, limit access, force password reset). Continuous Access Evaluation adds near-real-time revocation (summary-copilot-security-with-o365-e1-plus).

Underpins: zero-trust and control 1 of copilot-security-readiness. Also available in office-365-e1-plus.

Device grants: "Require device to be marked as compliant" reads state written by Intune or an onboarded compliance partner (device-compliance-signal-flow). "Require app protection policy" covers unenrolled BYOD (mdm-vs-mam). IP and named locations are Entra ID P1-only location signals, not trust signals (summary-intune-mdm-and-mam-for-m365-data).

Sources: summary-m365-e3-feature-map, summary-copilot-security-with-o365-e1-plus, summary-intune-mdm-and-mam-for-m365-data

10-notes/concepts/copilot-security-readi.title: Copilot security readiness
10-notes/concepts/copilot-security-readi.html:
Copilot security readiness

Idea: before (or while) rolling out microsoft-365-copilot, put five zero-trust controls in place. The licence tier sets how deep each control goes.

The five controls

# Control Baseline product
1 Govern access to Copilot microsoft-entra-id P1, conditional-access, MFA, CAE
2 Mitigate device risk microsoft-intune P1: app deployment, app protection, wipe
3 Protect against threats exchange-online-protection
4 Protect against data loss microsoft-purview DLP for email and files
5 Discover AI apps Entra Cloud App Discovery (400+ AI apps)

Staged rollout

  1. Web-grounded prompts first: Copilot Chat with enterprise-data-protection.
  2. Then Graph-grounded prompts: microsoft-365-copilot over organizational data.

Mature the five controls between the stages.

Good / better / best

Tier Positioning
office-365-e1-plus Baseline: Conditional Access, DLP for email and files, unified endpoint management
microsoft-365-e3 Core / jumping-off point: + Defender for Office 365 P1 (since July 2026; earlier material predates this), manual labels, standard eDiscovery and audit, block risky AI apps on windows-11-enterprise via microsoft-defender-for-endpoint P1
microsoft-365-e5 Best: Entra ID Protection risk-based access, automatic labels, communication compliance, Defender for Cloud Apps (block or sanction AI apps), Defender XDR

Talk-track use: open with "Copilot inherits your existing controls", then show where the customer sits on the ladder. Detail: summary-copilot-security-with-o365-e1-plus.

10-notes/concepts/device-compliance-sign.title: Device compliance signal flow (Intune → Entra → Conditional Access)
10-notes/concepts/device-compliance-sign.html:
Device compliance signal flow (Intune → Entra → Conditional Access)

Idea: three decoupled components make the device-based access decision for Microsoft 365.

  1. microsoft-intune evaluates device health and writes compliant or non-compliant onto the Entra ID device object.
  2. microsoft-entra-id stores that state.
  3. conditional-access enforces it at sign-in with the grant control "Require device to be marked as compliant". It does not call Intune at token time.

Consequences:

  • A UEM that cannot write the state, such as manageengine, cannot take part, whatever its posture checks are.
  • The microsoft-defender-for-endpoint risk score flows through the same path (Defender → Intune → Entra → CA) to block a high-risk device automatically.
  • On unenrolled BYOD, the equivalent control is "Require app protection policy" (mdm-vs-mam).

Source: summary-intune-mdm-and-mam-for-m365-data

10-notes/concepts/email-and-collaboratio.title: Email and collaboration protection layers
10-notes/concepts/email-and-collaboratio.html:
Email and collaboration protection layers

Idea: email and collaboration security comes in layers. Each layer adds detection depth and coverage.

  1. Baseline: exchange-online-protection (in office-365-e3 and office-365-e1-plus): multi-engine anti-malware, anti-spam, DLP.
  2. Threat protection (microsoft-defender-for-office-365 P1, included in O365/M365 E3 since July 2026 and in Business Premium): detonation (Safe Attachments), URL rewriting (Safe Links), impersonation anti-phishing, ZAP, extended to Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive.
  3. Investigation and response: real-time detections in P1. Plan 2 (E5) adds Threat Explorer, automated investigation and response, attack simulation training and Defender XDR integration (raw/2026-10-19-ms-learn-mdo-service-description.ref.md).

Sources: summary-m365-e3-feature-map, summary-mdo-plan1-feature-map

10-notes/concepts/enterprise-data-protec.title: Enterprise Data Protection (Copilot Chat)
10-notes/concepts/enterprise-data-protec.html:
Enterprise Data Protection (Copilot Chat)

Idea: when a user signs in to Microsoft Copilot (web chat) with a work account, the chat runs under enterprise data protection.

  • Prompts and responses are not used to train the underlying model.
  • Chat data is not retained Outdated. Under EDP, prompts and responses stay in the M365 service boundary and are stored in a hidden Substrate folder in the user's Exchange mailbox (confirmed by Jaspreet). They are logged, subject to the customer's retention policies and available for eDiscovery and Purview. The "not saved" wording belonged to the older commercial data protection (summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview). See claim-001.
  • Covered by the Data Protection Addendum and Product Terms (GDPR, ISO 27018). Available to anyone signed in with an Entra account, at no extra cost; the specific controls depend on the plan.
  • So: employees can safely include internal data in web-grounded prompts.

It is included for office-365-e1-plus users. It is distinct from Graph-grounded microsoft-365-copilot.

[!note] Resolved: EDP supersedes commercial data protection and adds logging, retention and eDiscovery (summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview).

Entry points: M365 Copilot app (pre-installed on Windows), m365copilot.com, Outlook, Teams, the Edge sidebar, Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

[!warning] Older guidance said E3 and E5 customers get Copilot "at no additional cost during preview". That refers to the old preview and is out of date; check current eligibility at aka.ms/Copilot/FAQ.

Rollout: this is stage 1 of the staged rollout in copilot-security-readiness.

Sources: summary-copilot-security-with-o365-e1-plus, summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview

Microsoft 365 licensing stack

Idea: Microsoft 365 suites are built from smaller suites. Explain them layer by layer, not as one long feature list.

Layer E3 component Role
Productivity and compliance office-365-e3 Apps, mail, files, collaboration, baseline DLP and retention
Identity and endpoint ems-e3 microsoft-entra-id P1, microsoft-intune, MIP P1

Below E3: office-365-e1-plus takes the identity and device layer (Entra ID P1, Intune P1) and adds DLP on top of web-only E1. It is a Zero Trust starter for emerging markets.

Why it matters: customers with O365 E3 and separate EMS E3 often miss the ME3-only extras. That gap is a common upsell or consolidation talking point. This is my inference, not stated in the source.

10-notes/concepts/mdm-vs-mam.title: MDM vs MAM
10-notes/concepts/mdm-vs-mam.html:
MDM vs MAM

Idea: there are two ways to manage endpoints. Pick one per device-ownership scenario.

MDM MAM
Controls Whole device Individual apps and their data
Typical fit Corporate-owned devices BYOD, unenrolled devices
Intune features (per source) Config profiles, compliance policies, patching, wipe App protection policies, Tunnel for MAM

Why MAM decides BYOD (summary-intune-mdm-and-mam-for-m365-data)

  • Apple caps MDM by enrolment type. Only Automated Device Enrollment (supervised, corporate) unlocks the full restriction set; User Enrollment gets a curated list.
  • Android Work Profile separates apps, not identities, and does nothing if the user declines enrolment.
  • Intune MAM works with no enrolment. It provides conditional launch, app PIN, selective wipe, multi-identity (work vs personal account in the same app), and cut/copy/paste, save-as and screen-capture controls. It is enforced by the CA grant "Require app protection policy".
  • Tunnel for MAM (per-app VPN on unenrolled iOS and Android) is in M365 E3 from July 2026 via Intune Plan 2 (microsoft-intune-suite).

Both are delivered by microsoft-intune. Related: device-compliance-signal-flow. Sources: summary-m365-e3-feature-map, summary-intune-mdm-and-mam-for-m365-data

10-notes/concepts/passwordless-authentic.title: Passwordless authentication
10-notes/concepts/passwordless-authentic.html:
Passwordless authentication

Idea: remove the password as a sign-in factor and replace it with phishing-resistant methods.

Method Where
windows-hello-for-business (PIN or biometric + TPM) Windows PCs
Microsoft Authenticator passwordless Mobile
FIDO2 security keys Shared or thin-client devices with no biometrics

What usually blocks it:

  1. Apps not yet integrated with microsoft-entra-id (still on ADFS or legacy auth)
  2. Devices without biometric hardware, which fall back to PIN or FIDO2

Why it matters: MFA blocks about 99% of identity attacks (summary-secure-remote-work-m365-e3), and passwordless removes the phishable factor entirely. It is part of verify-explicitly in zero-trust.

Sources: summary-passwordless-readiness-pattern, summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview

10-notes/concepts/windows-enterprise-ser.title: Windows Enterprise servicing model
10-notes/concepts/windows-enterprise-ser.html:
Windows Enterprise servicing model

Idea: Enterprise turns patching from a project into a managed service with more time and more control.

Lever Detail
Support window 36 months per annual feature update, vs 24 on Pro
Pinning Hold a feature update for up to 3 years (1,060 days, Jaspreet's figure). See windows-feature-update-pinning; public docs only say "36 months".
windows-autopatch Microsoft-managed rings, health gates, pause and rollback; now includes the WUfB deployment service
Expedite Bypass rings and deferrals for a zero-day KB; fleet compliant in hours
Hotpatch Monthly security fixes applied in memory with no reboot
Reports Release health, device readiness, compatibility risks
Connected Cache Local caching for low-bandwidth sites

[!warning] Do not mix the efficiency figures. Two different Forrester studies give different Autopatch numbers. Name the source each time:

  • 60–80% less patching time (Forrester TEI study commissioned by Microsoft, 2024)
  • 45% / 95% / 80% for monthly, feature and reporting effort (Forrester projected TEI study commissioned by Microsoft, 2023)

10-notes/concepts/windows-virtualization.title: Windows Enterprise virtualization rights
10-notes/concepts/windows-virtualization.html:
Windows Enterprise virtualization rights

Idea: Windows Enterprise E3 is per user. Each user may run up to 5 Windows instances at once, physical or virtual. VDI access rights are included, so no extra CALs are needed.

  • Instances: local windows-11-enterprise, Windows 365 Cloud PC, Azure Virtual Desktop, on-premises VDI under VDA, and LTSC for special-purpose devices.
  • Contrast:
    • Windows Pro is a device licence with no VDI rights.
    • Enterprise + Software Assurance is per device, with VDA only (no AVD or W365 rights, no cloud services).
  • Precise wording, from the public Product Terms (raw/2026-10-19-windows-use-rights.ref.md):
    • "5 instances" means Windows can be activated on up to 5 concurrent physical devices per user, through Entra ID-based activation.
    • AVD VMs don't count toward those 5.
    • Separately, there are rights to 4 local virtual OSEs and remote access to up to 4 virtual OSEs.
    • The licensed user must be the primary user of at least one device with a qualifying OS (Pro).
  • Windows 365: it is an access right only. The Cloud PC still needs its own Windows 365 subscription.
  • Via M365 F3: Windows Enterprise E3 excludes MDOP, LTSC and Autopatch, per the Windows licensing overview. This conflicts with the Autopatch prerequisites; see windows-autopatch#claim-002.

[!warning] Don't say "5 environments: local, AVD, W365, VDI" to customers. The terms count 5 activated devices; AVD is separate, W365 is licensed separately, and VDA is a separate right.

  • Customer question: "Do you buy CALs for your VDI?"

Sources: summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview, summary-windows-enterprise-e3-licensing-2023

10-notes/concepts/zero-trust.title: Zero Trust
10-notes/concepts/zero-trust.html:
Zero Trust

Idea: a security strategy, not a product, built on three principles: verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach. In short: "never trust, always verify".

  • Microsoft's AI framing: security recommendations for AI are anchored in Zero Trust, and building those protections now prepares a tenant for Copilot.
  • In M365: identity (microsoft-entra-id, conditional-access), devices (microsoft-intune), threats (exchange-online-protection, microsoft-defender-for-office-365, microsoft-defender-for-endpoint), data (microsoft-purview) and apps (Cloud App Discovery).
  • Applied to Copilot: copilot-security-readiness
  • Applied to work-from-home in M365 E3: summary-secure-remote-work-m365-e3. Note that Identity Protection and just-in-time access are often wrongly mapped to E3.
  • On the device: windows-hello-for-business, Credential Guard, TPM 2.0 (windows-11-enterprise); device-compliance-signal-flow; passwordless-authentication

Source: summary-copilot-security-with-o365-e1-plus

10-notes/entities/always-on-vpn.title: Always On VPN
10-notes/entities/always-on-vpn.html:
Always On VPN

What it is: The built-in Windows VPN platform (VPNv2 CSP / ProfileXML) that connects automatically and stays connected. A user tunnel carries user access after sign-in. An optional device tunnel connects before sign-in for management and first logon. It's Microsoft's replacement for DirectAccess.

What it is

User tunnel Device tunnel
Connects After user signs in Before sign-in (pre-logon)
Protocols IKEv2, SSTP (Automatic fallback) IKEv2 only, no SSTP fallback
Auth EAP: user certs, windows-hello-for-business, MFA via RADIUS, conditional-access short-lived certs Machine certificate
Join state Domain, workgroup or microsoft-entra-id joined Domain-joined only
Third-party (UWP plug-in) control ✅ ❌
Routing Split or force Split tunnel only

How it works

  • Profiles are deployed via microsoft-intune, Configuration Manager, PowerShell/WMI bridge or third-party MDM. The device tunnel must be created in the LOCAL SYSTEM context.
  • Infrastructure is either Windows Server RRAS + NPS (RADIUS) + internal PKI, or third-party IKEv2 gateways / UWP plug-ins (Cisco, Palo Alto GlobalProtect, Fortinet, etc.).
  • Features: app/name-based triggers, trusted network detection, traffic and app filters, per-app VPN, NRPT, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6, and VPN conditional-access (Entra issues short-lived certs).
  • Device tunnel traffic filters restrict it to management servers. Enabling filters blocks inbound "manage-out" traffic.

Requirements & licensing

Pro / Pro Edu / SE Enterprise Education
Windows VPN platform / user tunnel ✅ ✅ ✅
Device tunnel (pre-logon) ❌ ✅ ✅
Licence Pro licence covers VPN E3/E5 (Enterprise edition needed for device tunnel) A3/A5

[!warning] Disputed vault claim resolved: "Always-On VPN user tunnel is a Windows Enterprise differentiator" is FALSE. Microsoft Learn's device tunnel and Always On VPN overview pages say the user tunnel "is available in all Windows editions", and that only the device tunnel is limited to domain-joined Enterprise or Education devices. The Windows VPN technical guide's licensing table also shows VPN as Yes for Pro and for all licences. Only the device tunnel is an Enterprise/Education differentiator.

[!warning] The licensing overview is internally inconsistent. It lists "Always-On VPN device tunnel" as a unique Enterprise feature, but its edition table marks "Always On VPN" as Pro ✅ / Enterprise ✅. Read it as: the AOVPN platform works on Pro, but the device tunnel doesn't.

[!question] The device-tunnel docs still say "Windows 10 Enterprise or Education 1709+". The assumption that this carries over to Windows 11 Enterprise/Education is inferred from the "Applies to: Windows 11" banner, not stated explicitly.

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Pre-logon device tunnel enables first-time sign-in without cached credentials, password reset, GPO/Windows Update/ConfigMgr reach and manage-out for remote devices. This is the real Enterprise upsell.
  • Works with windows-hello-for-business, MFA and conditional-access, so it fits a zero-trust approach.
  • DirectAccess is deprecated (KB5103659, June 2026). It's still available in Server 2025, but AOVPN is the recommended migration path.

Limitations & gotchas

  • No third-party control of the device tunnel. Its NRPT is usable only if no user tunnel exists.
  • The device tunnel needs domain join, so it doesn't fit Entra-only (cloud-native) devices.
  • SSTP can't be configured by MDM directly (only via the Automatic protocol).
  • RRAS with device tunnel: enable IKEv2 machine-cert auth and restrict it to an internal root CA.
  • Many organizations now compare AOVPN with SSE/ZTNA options.

10-notes/entities/bitlocker-advanced-man.title: BitLocker Advanced (Modern) Management
10-notes/entities/bitlocker-advanced-man.html:
BitLocker Advanced (Modern) Management

What it is: Cloud/MDM control of BitLocker and BitLocker To Go through the BitLocker CSP and microsoft-intune. It covers enforcing ciphers and startup authentication, silent encryption, recovery-key escrow to microsoft-entra-id, key rotation and compliance reporting, with no on-premises tooling (it replaces MBAM-style tools).

What it is

  • Enablement means turning on full-volume encryption, including automatic device encryption.
  • Management means centrally enforcing how BitLocker is configured, plus reporting and recovery. Microsoft documents these two with different licence rules.

How it works (key Intune/CSP controls)

Control CSP node / Intune setting
Cipher per drive type (XTS-AES 128/256, AES-CBC) EncryptionMethodByDriveType (default XTS-AES 128)
Silent / zero-touch encryption RequireDeviceEncryption=1 + AllowWarningForOtherDiskEncryption=0 (+ AllowStandardUserEncryption=1)
Startup auth TPM+PIN / startup key SystemDrivesRequireStartupAuthentication
PIN length (4–20) / enhanced PIN SystemDrivesMinimumPINLength, SystemDrivesEnhancedPIN
Escrow key before encrypting SystemDrivesRecoveryOptions → "Do not enable BitLocker until recovery info is stored"
Recovery password rotation ConfigureRecoveryPasswordRotation, RotateRecoveryPasswords, plus the Intune BitLocker key rotation remote action
BitLocker To Go: deny write to unprotected removable drives RemovableDrivesRequireEncryption (optionally cross-org deny via IdentificationField)
Compliance / reporting Status/DeviceEncryptionStatus bitmask, Intune Encryption report, compliance policy plus conditional-access
  • Silent encryption needs Entra join/hybrid join, TPM, native UEFI, Secure Boot and WinRE, and no TPM PIN/startup key. TPM+PIN and silent encryption are mutually exclusive.
  • Admins view keys in the Intune portal. Every key view is audited, and users can self-serve keys through Company Portal or My Account. Entra ID holds a maximum of 200 keys per device.

Requirements & licensing

Windows Pro / Pro Edu / SE Windows Enterprise Windows Education
BitLocker enablement – edition ✅ ✅ ✅
BitLocker enablement – licence ✅ Pro licence ✅ E3/E5 ✅ A3/A5
BitLocker management – edition (works technically) ✅ ✅ ✅
BitLocker management – licence entitlement ❌ Pro licence alone ✅ Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (microsoft-365-e3/microsoft-365-e5, also M365 F3) ✅ A3/A5

[!warning] Vault claim "advanced BitLocker management is an Enterprise (edition) differentiator" is only partly true. Public docs show the BitLocker CSP works on Pro (since Windows 10 1809), and the licensing overview marks "Modern BitLocker Management" as Pro ✅ / Enterprise ✅ for edition. The differentiator is the user licence (Windows Enterprise E3/E5 or A3/A5), not the Enterprise edition/SKU. The CSP doc says managing BitLocker via CSP, beyond enabling/disabling it with RequireDeviceEncryption, needs one of those licences "regardless of your management platform". This is a licensing requirement and isn't technically enforced on the device. Correct wording: "Requires Windows Enterprise E3/E5 licensing; runs on Pro or Enterprise edition."

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Removes on-premises MBAM/key-escrow infrastructure. Recovery keys live in Entra ID with audit and self-service.
  • Rotating keys after use stops a key that a helpdesk read out from being reused.
  • Encryption state feeds compliance and conditional-access, a zero-trust device-health signal.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Most settings apply only when encryption starts. Changing the cipher on an already-encrypted drive means decrypting and re-encrypting.
  • Silent encryption ignores warnings about third-party encryption, which risks data loss. Inventory first.
  • Security baselines that enable a TPM startup PIN block silent enablement.
  • Some settings are GPO-only (e.g., Network Unlock, PCR profiles).

[!question] Microsoft doesn't publish per-setting licence enforcement. Assume every CSP setting except RequireDeviceEncryption falls under the E3/A3 licensing note.

10-notes/entities/credential-guard.title: Credential Guard
10-notes/entities/credential-guard.html:
Credential Guard

What it is: A Windows security feature that uses virtualization-based security (VBS) to isolate credential secrets (NTLM password hashes, Kerberos TGTs and app-stored domain credentials) away from the normal OS. Even admin-level malware can't pull them out. It's a core windows-11-enterprise differentiator.

What it is

  • Isolates LSA secrets in a VBS-protected process (LSAIso.exe) that only privileged system software can reach.
  • Mitigates pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket credential theft and the common tools used in targeted attacks.
  • Remote Credential Guard is a related feature. It protects credentials over RDP by sending Kerberos requests back to the client, so credentials never land on the target host.

How it works

  • NTLM, Kerberos-derived credentials and Credential Manager secrets run in an isolated VBS environment.
  • Default-on: from Windows 11 22H2 (and Server 2025 for domain-joined non-DCs), eligible devices get Credential Guard enabled automatically. Eligible means licensed, hardware-capable and not explicitly disabled. VBS gets turned on along with it.
  • Default enablement uses no UEFI lock, so admins can turn it off remotely. If you set a UEFI lock manually, a registry change can't disable it.
  • If you disabled it explicitly before upgrading to 22H2, the upgrade keeps it off.
  • Configure it with microsoft-intune (settings catalog/CSP), Group Policy or the registry.

Requirements & licensing

Pro / Pro Edu / SE Enterprise Education
Credential Guard edition support ❌ ✅ ✅
Licence that grants it — (Pro licence: No) Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (e.g. via microsoft-365-e3/microsoft-365-e5) Education A3/A5
Remote Credential Guard ✅ ✅ ✅
  • Hardware: VBS is required. Secure Boot is also listed as required, although default enablement can bring VBS up without it. TPM 1.2/2.0 (discrete or firmware) and UEFI lock are recommended.
  • VMs: works only on Hyper-V Generation 2 VMs, and the host needs an IOMMU. Gen 1 VMs aren't supported.
  • Pro edge case: a Pro device that previously ran Credential Guard, for example after downgrading from Enterprise, may still have it switched on.

[!question] The overview lists Secure Boot under required features, but the default-enablement note says Secure Boot isn't a hard prerequisite for VBS. Treat Secure Boot as "strongly recommended / required for full guarantees".

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Blocks lateral movement by stopping hash and ticket theft from LSASS, a key zero-trust "assume breach" control.
  • Enterprise and Education devices get it by default on Windows 11 22H2+, so customers often already have it with no extra project.
  • Pairs with windows-hello-for-business and passwordless-authentication to reduce credential exposure overall.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Breaks apps that need Kerberos DES, Kerberos unconstrained delegation, Kerberos TGT extraction or NTLMv1.
  • Apps that use MS-CHAPv2, Digest, CredSSP or credential delegation get prompted for credentials and expose them to risk. This affects older VPN/Wi-Fi setups using MS-CHAPv2/PEAP.
  • Not recommended on domain controllers (no added security). Not supported on Exchange Server.
  • Doesn't protect the AD database or local SAM.
  • Remote Credential Guard requires Kerberos (no NTLM fallback) and an AD-joined target. It doesn't work through RD Gateway/Connection Broker, and it isn't recommended for helpdesk use (use Restricted Admin instead).
  • Test app compatibility before relying on default enablement.

10-notes/entities/exchange-online-protec.title: Exchange Online Protection
10-notes/entities/exchange-online-protec.html:
Exchange Online Protection

Microsoft's cloud email filtering service against spam, malware, phishing and other email threats. It is the baseline in every Exchange Online plan, including office-365-e1-plus and office-365-e3.

10-notes/entities/organizational-message.title: Organizational Messages
10-notes/entities/organizational-message.html:
Organizational Messages

What it is: Organizational messages let IT and comms teams push branded, targeted, scheduled messages straight into Windows (lock screen, taskbar, notifications) and Microsoft 365 surfaces, managed from one place in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Typical uses: onboarding, Copilot/app adoption, tech-change notices, and urgent outage alerts.

How it works

  • Where to author: Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Organizational messages (Manage messages · Create a message · Review activity). The old Intune entry point now points to this experience.
  • Roles: Organizational Messages Writer creates; Organizational Messages Approver approves custom messages (can't approve own). Recipients need no role.
  • Wizard: Objective (adoption, onboarding, sustainability, tech updates) → Location → Template (Microsoft pre-made + your logo/URL, or fully custom) → Customize → Recipients → Schedule → Finish.
  • Locations: Windows Spotlight (lock screen), Windows taskbar, Notification Center, Microsoft Teams notifications, and email (8 fixed, non-customizable Copilot templates).
  • Targeting: Entra groups; advanced targeting by company, department, location (via Adoption Score group-level aggregates) and usage (e.g., inactive Copilot users, 28/30-day lookback). Teams only supports Entra groups.
  • Schedule: start/end dates + repeat frequency; a dismissed/ignored message reappears; a clicked message won't reappear for a year.
  • Urgent messages: taskbar/Notifications only, Entra groups only, sent once ASAP; cached up to 24 h for offline devices.
  • Reporting: impressions (messages seen), clicks, click-through rate, time-series charts, CSV export. Email open tracking is being removed.
  • Device policy (microsoft-intune settings catalog, Experience): allow Enable delivery of organizational messages, Windows Spotlight (+ Action Center, lock screen), Windows Tips; set Disable Cloud Optimized Content to Disabled; make sure no device-restriction profile blocks Spotlight/Tips.

Requirements & licensing

Home / Pro Enterprise / Education
Windows surfaces (Spotlight, taskbar, notifications) ❌ Not supported ✅ Windows 11 24H2/25H2 Enterprise; taskbar needs KB5094126
Device join — microsoft-entra-id joined or hybrid joined
Pre-made templates Teams/email surfaces only ✅
Custom messages + advanced targeting Tenant needs M365 E3/E5, O365 E3/E5 or Windows Enterprise E3/E5 same
  • Windows licensing overview lists org messages as a Windows Enterprise-only cloud feature (not on Pro). See microsoft-365-e3.
  • Firewall: allow fd.api.orgmsg.microsoft.com and ris.prod.api.personalization.ideas.microsoft.com.

[!warning] Vault/legacy notes say "Windows 11 22H2+" and "Entra-joined only". Current Learn (updated 2026-07-22) says 24H2/25H2 Enterprise and now also supports hybrid join; older Learn versions explicitly excluded hybrid-joined devices.

[!question] Older (Intune-era) docs listed the Get Started app, and Adoption Score messages appear in Outlook/Word/Excel/PowerPoint. Current org-messages doc doesn't list Get Started — confirm whether it's retired.

[!warning] No public Microsoft source quantifies how much more effective org messages are than email. Don't quote an effectiveness multiplier to customers without a citation.

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Reaches users where they are (lock screen/taskbar) rather than a crowded inbox; measurable via CTR.
  • Governed: approval workflow, role separation, central inventory.
  • Drives Copilot/M365 adoption with usage-based targeting.
  • A visible, tangible windows-11-enterprise benefit for comms/HR stakeholders, not just IT.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Security baselines/restrictive profiles that block Spotlight or consumer content silently stop delivery.
  • New tenants: 36–64 h after Entra onboarding; dormant tenants: 24–48 h to initialize targeting.
  • Delivery not guaranteed for offline devices; message display can lag hours.
  • Email channel is template-only.

10-notes/entities/personal-data-encrypti.title: Personal Data Encryption (PDE)
10-notes/entities/personal-data-encrypti.html:
Personal Data Encryption (PDE)

What it is: File-level encryption built into Windows 11. The keys are tied to the user's windows-hello-for-business sign-in. Protected files open only after the owner signs in with Windows Hello, and the keys are discarded at sign-out (or 1 minute after lock at Level 2).

What it is

  • Encrypts individual files, not volumes. Uses AES-CBC with a 256-bit key.
  • PDE for known folders (Windows 11 24H2+) automatically encrypts the user's Desktop, Documents and Pictures.
  • Apps and scripts can also protect specific content through the PDE APIs, once the policy is enabled.

How it works

  • Level 1: data stays readable while the device is locked and becomes unreadable after sign-out.
  • Level 2: data becomes unreadable one minute after lock as well as after sign-out.
  • Access is denied after a password or FIDO2 sign-in (not Windows Hello), over UNC paths, in RDP sessions and for other local users.
  • vs BitLocker: BitLocker releases keys at boot and protects the whole volume. PDE releases keys at Windows Hello sign-in and protects files. Microsoft says to use both because neither replaces the other. See bitlocker-advanced-management.
  • vs EFS: EFS protects files with certificates, while PDE protects its keys with Windows Hello for Business.
  • Configuration: in microsoft-intune, use Endpoint security → Disk encryption → Personal Data Encryption profile, the settings catalog (PDE category) or the PDE CSP (./User/Vendor/MSFT/PDE/...). PDE is off by default.

Requirements & licensing

Pro / Pro Edu / SE Enterprise Education
PDE edition support ❌ ✅ ✅
Licence that grants it — Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (microsoft-365-e3/microsoft-365-e5) Education A3/A5
  • Windows 11 22H2+ (known folders 24H2+).
  • Device must be microsoft-entra-id joined or hybrid joined. Domain-joined-only devices aren't supported.
  • Users must sign in with Windows Hello. ARSO (automatic restart sign-on) must be disabled.
  • If the prerequisites aren't met, Windows falls back to DPAPI.

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Protects data after boot (lost unlocked/sleeping laptop, multi-user devices, admin snooping), which BitLocker doesn't cover on its own.
  • No extra password: the Windows Hello sign-in unlocks the data, which fits passwordless-authentication and zero-trust.
  • One of the few OS features that is strictly Enterprise/Education (the licensing overview marks Pro ❌), so it's a clean windows-11-enterprise upsell.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Data loss risk: a destructive Windows Hello PIN reset or TPM reset loses the keys permanently, and content can only come back from backup. Deploy the Windows Hello for Business PIN reset service (non-destructive) and OneDrive backup first.
  • Hardening recommendations: disable hibernation, kernel and user-mode crash dumps / WER, and the connected-standby password-delay option, because these can expose keys.
  • Not accessible over RDP or network shares. Password-only users lose access.
  • Disabling PDE auto-decrypts known-folder content but not API-protected files, which need cipher /d. Once a user manually decrypts a file, they can't re-protect it.

[!question] Behaviour with OneDrive Known Folder Move and sync clients wasn't fully checked against the PDE FAQ. Verify before customer guidance.

10-notes/entities/point-in-time-restore.title: Point-in-time Restore for Windows
10-notes/entities/point-in-time-restore.html:
Point-in-time Restore for Windows

What it is: Point-in-time restore (PITR) rolls an entire Windows 11 PC back to the exact state it was in at a recent restore point — OS, apps, settings and local files — in minutes, using Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) snapshots stored on the device. It is a Windows Resiliency Initiative companion to quick-machine-recovery.

How it works

  • Capture: automatic background VSS snapshots, about every 24 h by default; no user data is excluded.
  • Window: points older than ~72 h are pruned; also pruned when VSS max usage is hit or free space ≤20 GB (oldest first); a VSS failure can wipe all points.
  • Storage: counts against system reserved storage; max usage default 2% of disk (2–50 GB), not pre-allocated; shared with any other VSS tool (System Restore, third-party rollback).
  • Restore flow (WinRE only, in preview): enter WinRE (auto after boot failures, or Settings > Recovery > Advanced startup) → Troubleshoot > Point-in-time restore → enter BitLocker recovery key → pick point → acknowledge risks → Restore → reboots into Windows.
  • Manage: Settings > System > Recovery > Point-in-time restore; Recovery CSP PointInTimeRestore node (EnablePointInTimeRestore, SetMaxDiskUsage 2048–51200 MB, SetRestorePointFrequency / SetRestorePointRetention in minutes); vssadmin to list/delete points.

On/Off by edition (below) On/Off Home, Pro, Enterprise
Frequency ~24 h 4/6/12/16/24 h Enterprise only
Retention ~72 h 4–72 h Enterprise only
Max usage 2% of disk 2–50 GB Home, Pro, Enterprise

Requirements & licensing

Home / Pro (unmanaged) Enterprise / Education (and managed Pro)

Tune frequency/retention No Yes (Enterprise)
CSP applicability Pro Enterprise, Education, IoT Enterprise/LTSC

[!question] Learn still says restore "in preview" can only start from WinRE — confirm GA status and whether remote/Intune-triggered restore is planned.

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Undo a bad update, driver, misconfiguration or user error on a physical PC without reimaging.
  • Faster than rebuild + data restore; OneDrive-synced data stays current.
  • Enterprise-only tuning (e.g., 4-hourly points) is a concrete windows-11-enterprise differentiator.
  • Pairs with quick-machine-recovery (Microsoft-pushed fixes) and bitlocker-advanced-management (key escrow for the restore step).

Limitations & gotchas

  • Data loss: everything local after the point is gone — including passwords, certs, keys, and possibly recent security updates/policies; re-validate posture after restore.
  • Needs free space ≥ total size of restore points to complete.
  • OS volume only; no export/mount of points; points don't survive an edition change (e.g., Home→Pro).
  • EFS-encrypted files block restore; power loss mid-restore can brick the OS.
  • Known issues: Outlook .ost mismatch (rebuild cache), Recall disabled until re-confirmed, BitLocker auto-unlock lost on data volumes.
  • Timing is approximate (sleep/off devices miss captures).

vs System Restore: System Restore is event/manual-triggered, Control Panel-managed, covers system files/settings, indefinite retention; PITR is scheduled, full-state, ≤72 h, remotely manageable, lower storage impact.

vs Windows 365 PITR: W365 Cloud PC restore is always on, keeps short-term, long-term and manual points up to ~1 month in cloud storage, and can be shared across Windows 365/Azure; client PITR is local, short-term only.

10-notes/entities/quick-machine-recovery.title: Quick Machine Recovery
10-notes/entities/quick-machine-recovery.html:
Quick Machine Recovery

What it is: Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets a Windows 11 PC that is stuck in a boot-failure loop fix itself: WinRE gets on the network and pulls a targeted remediation from Windows Update, with no hands-on IT. It is a flagship capability of Microsoft's Windows Resiliency Initiative (WRI), built in response to widespread outages such as the July 2024 incident.

How it works

  • Trigger: repeated boot failures → device boots into WinRE automatically (users can also launch it from WinRE: Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Quick machine recovery).
  • Connect: WinRE joins wired Ethernet or WPA/WPA2 password Wi-Fi (no enterprise/802.1X Wi-Fi yet); can reuse saved Wi-Fi profiles (NetworkSettings/Wifi/ReuseWifiSavedOnDevice).
  • Remediate: scans Windows Update; if a fix exists it's downloaded, applied and the PC restarts. If it fails, the loop repeats; if nothing found, the user is sent to classic recovery options.
  • Two settings:
Setting On Off
Cloud remediation Uses network + Windows Update in WinRE Falls back to local Startup Repair
Auto remediation Scans automatically; one-time or looped retries Requires manual intervention
  • Retry tuning (CSP): SetRetryInterval 0–4320 min (0 = scan once); SetTimeToReboot 1–4320 min (max 72 h, ≥ retry interval).
  • Config channels: Recovery CSP (./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Recovery/QuickMachineRecovery/...) via microsoft-intune/MDM; reagentc /setrecoverysettings with XML; Settings > System > Recovery; GPO only on Windows Server 2025.
  • Test mode: reagentc /SetRecoveryTestmode + reagentc /BootToRe simulates a crash and remediation — currently Insider Experimental channel only.

  • Print-job pool: jobs are counted per document, regardless of pages or copies. Each licence adds jobs to one tenant-wide monthly pool; there is no per-user cap.
Licence Jobs added per month

10-notes/entities/windows-autopatch.title: Windows Autopatch
10-notes/entities/windows-autopatch.html:
Windows Autopatch

A Microsoft service that automates Windows and Office update rollout. It is listed under windows-11-enterprise.

  • Ring-based patching
  • A measurable update-currency target (SLO)
  • Break-glass controls: pause and rollback

How it works

  • Division of labour: you enroll devices. Microsoft evaluates and selects updates, builds and maintains rings, schedules, deploys, monitors, pauses and rolls back.
  • Scope: Windows quality, feature, driver and firmware updates, plus M365 Apps, Edge and Teams.
  • Example rings: Test 1% → First 10% → Fast 20% → Broad 69%, with health gates.
  • Now absorbs the Windows Update for Business deployment service, in one dashboard in the Intune admin center with no feature loss (summary-windows-11-enterprise-overview).
  • Requires microsoft-intune. It runs on Pro hardware but is licensed through Enterprise E3/E5.

Value claims

These measure different things, so always cite which one you use. See windows-enterprise-servicing.

  • 60–80% less patching time (Forrester TEI study commissioned by Microsoft, 2024)
  • 45% / 95% / 80% less effort on monthly, feature and reporting work (Forrester projected TEI study commissioned by Microsoft, 2023)

Licensing and prerequisites (Microsoft Learn, updated Feb 2026)

  • Eligible licences: M365 Business Premium; Windows Education A3/A5; Windows Enterprise E3/E5, included in M365 F3, E3 or E5; Windows Enterprise E3/E5 VDA. F3 and E3+ get the same features, including support requests; Business Premium and A3+ do not get support requests.

[!warning] Conflicting Microsoft pages on F3 (claim-002): the Windows licensing overview (updated May 2026) says Windows E3 delivered through M365 F3 excludes Autopatch, which contradicts this prerequisites page. Check the Product Terms before telling an F3 customer.

  • Needs: Entra ID P1 or P2 plus Intune. Devices must be Intune-managed or co-managed (Windows Update and Device configuration workloads set to Intune or Pilot Intune), and must have checked in within the last 28 days.
  • Corporate-owned devices only. Windows BYOD is blocked at registration.
  • Editions: Windows 10/11 Pro, Education, Enterprise, Pro for Workstations and IoT Enterprise. On LTSC, quality updates only.
  • Diagnostic data: at least Required level for the deployment protections.

10-notes/entities/windows-enterprise-ser.title: Windows 11 Servicing Lifecycle (Enterprise vs Pro, LTSC, Windows 10 ESU)
10-notes/entities/windows-enterprise-ser.html:
Windows 11 Servicing Lifecycle (Enterprise vs Pro, LTSC, Windows 10 ESU)

What it is: Windows 11 follows the Modern Lifecycle Policy. There is one feature update a year, in H2, plus cumulative monthly quality updates. How long each version gets security fixes depends on the edition. Enterprise/Education gets 12 months more than Pro.

How it works

  • Cadence: annual feature update in the second half of the year (24H2, 25H2, 26H2…). Security (B) updates ship on the 2nd Tuesday of each month, with optional D-week previews.
  • To stay supported, a device must move to a newer version before its version reaches end of servicing.
  • 26H1 is a special release for new early-2026 hardware only. It isn't offered as an in-place update and doesn't support IoT Enterprise or hotpatch.

General Availability Channel

Edition Support per version
Enterprise, Education, IoT Enterprise, Enterprise multi-session 36 months
Pro, Pro Education, Pro for Workstations, Home, SE 24 months
Version GA End – Pro/Home End – Enterprise/Edu
23H2 2023-10-31 ended 2026-11-10
24H2 2024-10-01 ended 2027-10-12
25H2 2025-09-30 2027-10-12 2028-10-10
26H2 2026-09-29 2028-10-10 2029-10-09

LTSC (Fixed Lifecycle)

  • Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024 (= 24H2 code base, GA 2024-10-01): 5 years, ending Oct 2029, with no extended support.
  • Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 2024: mainstream to Oct 2029 plus extended to Oct 2034, about 10 years.
  • LTSC is meant for special-purpose devices (medical, ATM, kiosk/control). It has no feature updates, and inbox apps and Edge are excluded.

Windows 10

  • End of support: 14 Oct 2025 (22H2 was the final version). Since then there are no security/quality updates or support without ESU.
  • ESU (commercial): paid yearly per device, USD 61 in Year One, doubling each year, max 3 years. Years are cumulative: joining in Year Two means paying for Year One too. Devices must run 22H2.
  • ESU is free for Windows 10 VMs in Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop, Azure VMs and other Azure-family hosts. Windows 10 endpoints connecting to Windows 365 Cloud PCs are also entitled for up to 3 years. See windows-virtualization-rights.
  • ESU covers Critical/Important security fixes only. It includes no new features and no general tech support.

Requirements & licensing

Need Licence / edition
36-month servicing Windows 11 Enterprise/Education (e.g., microsoft-365-e3, microsoft-365-e5, A3/A5)
LTSC 2024 Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC (volume licensing) or IoT Enterprise LTSC (OEM)
Windows 10 ESU Separate per-device ESU purchase (VL), or free via cloud/virtual entitlements

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Enterprise lets IT skip a year and upgrade every 2–3 years. Pro forces a yearly cycle. This pairs with windows-feature-update-pinning.
  • Windows 10 holdouts should either budget rising ESU costs or move to Windows 11 / Windows 365.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Pinning doesn't extend support.
  • LTSC isn't a general desktop SKU, and Autopatch doesn't upgrade it. Use LTSC media or ConfigMgr OSD.

[!warning] LTSC 2024 end dates differ by a day between sources. Release information shows 2029-10-09 and 2034-10-10, while Lifecycle product pages (Pacific Time) show Oct 10 2029 and Oct 11 2034. Treat these as the same Patch Tuesday boundary.

[!question] The ESU FAQ says "Year One starts in November 2025" while support ended 14 Oct 2025. The exact coverage-period start isn't clear from this page.

10-notes/entities/windows-expedited-upda.title: Expedited Windows Quality Updates (Intune / Autopatch)
10-notes/entities/windows-expedited-upda.html:
Expedited Windows Quality Updates (Intune / Autopatch)

What it is: An Intune expedite policy forces one specific Windows quality update onto targeted devices as fast as possible. It ignores the normal ring deferrals, so you can close a zero-day without pausing or rewriting your monthly update rings.

How it works

  • Create it under Devices › Windows updates › Quality updates › Create › Expedite policy in microsoft-intune. The same capability is exposed in windows-autopatch.
  • You pick one update per policy, identified by release date. The list shows the two latest security releases (B or OOB). Non-security D/OOB releases appear only when no newer security update exists, and they apply to Windows 11 only.
  • Windows Update checks applicability per device. Devices already on that update or a newer one are skipped. A newer superseding update may be installed if no deferral blocks it.
  • Installation starts after the device's next scan/check-in.
  • Restart deadline: 0, 1 or 2 days (≈ immediate, 24 h, 48 h). After the deadline the restart is forced, even inside active hours. A manual restart before then cancels the forced one.
  • The policy is one-off. Ongoing servicing stays with update rings or quality update policies.
  • Reporting: Reports › Windows Updates (Expedited Quality updates summary + Windows Expedited Update Report) and Devices › Monitor › Expedited quality update policies with alerts. States run Pending → Offering → Installing (download/install/restart) → Installed.

Requirements & licensing

Area Requirement
Licence Intune Plan 1 + Windows licence with Autopatch entitlement: Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (incl. microsoft-365-e3/microsoft-365-e5/F3), Education A3/A5, E3/E5 VDA, or M365 Business Premium
Editions Pro, Pro Education, Enterprise, Education (not LTSC)
Join Intune-managed; microsoft-entra-id joined or hybrid joined
Diagnostic data At least Required level; tenant must allow Intune to use Windows diagnostic data (for reports)
Services Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant (wlidsvc) running; internet access to Intune, WU and Autopatch endpoints
Update Health Tools Needed before 24H2 (KB4023057). Remove on 24H2+
Clouds Public and GCC

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Faster response to an actively exploited vulnerability, with no need to rebuild rings or pause updates.
  • Device-level reporting gives evidence for security and audit teams.
  • Pairs well with windows-hotpatch (fewer restarts) as part of a zero-trust "assume breach, patch fast" posture.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Only eligible updates can be expedited. You can't pick an arbitrary historical KB.
  • A 0-day deadline can disrupt users. Use it only for critical cases.
  • Legacy GPO/MDM settings can block expedite: WSUS URL (CorpWuURL), AutoUpdateCfg, DeferFeatureUpdates, Disable Dual Scan, pre-release builds, and "turn off all notifications". Reset them to defaults.
  • Deleting the policy doesn't uninstall updates that already installed. Cancelling an in-progress install isn't guaranteed.
  • Expedite overrides only the deferral for the chosen update, not deferrals on other versions.

[!warning] Licensing wording varies between pages. The current Intune quality-update page requires an "Autopatch entitlement". A third-party summary lists Business Premium/A3/E3/E5/VDA, and that list matches the Autopatch prerequisites. Pro is a supported edition, but a licence such as Windows E3 or Business Premium is still needed.

10-notes/entities/windows-feature-update.title: Windows Feature Update Pinning (Intune Feature Update Policy)
10-notes/entities/windows-feature-update.html:
Windows Feature Update Pinning (Intune Feature Update Policy)

What it is: A Feature updates policy in microsoft-intune / windows-autopatch holds ("pins") devices on a chosen Windows version, such as 24H2 or 25H2, or moves them up to that version and no further. Users get a stable feature set while apps are validated.

How it works

  • Each policy targets one Windows version. Only versions still in support can be selected.
  • Devices below that version upgrade to it. Devices already on a newer version stay where they are, because the policy never downgrades.
  • The pin persists until you change or remove the policy. An update-ring pause, by contrast, expires after 35 days.
  • If several policies target a device, Windows Update offers the latest applicable version. Required beats Optional.
  • Rollout options: ASAP, scheduled start, or gradual rollout. You can also make the update Optional for users, which needs the Autopatch licence.
  • Set the update ring Feature update deferral to 0 and don't pause feature updates in rings. Otherwise deferrals and policies clash.
  • Readiness reports: the Windows feature update device readiness report (per device: Low/Medium/High risk, Replace device) and the compatibility risks report (top apps/drivers across the org). Both use Windows diagnostic data and can lag by up to ~52 hours.

How long can you stay pinned?

Edition Servicing per annual release
Enterprise, Education, IoT Enterprise, multi-session 36 months
Pro, Pro Education, Pro for Workstations, Home 24 months
  • Example (Enterprise): 24H2 is serviced until 2027-10-12 and 25H2 until 2028-10-10.
  • In the policy list Intune shows a Support End Date (Enterprise/Education dates), with Support Ending status inside two months of that date. After it, the policy shows Not supported and the version no longer deploys.

[!question] The vault owner's "up to 3 years (1,060 days)" is not publicly documented. Learn states 36 months, and real 24H2/25H2 windows are ~1,106 days from GA. 1,060 days may be a pin length counted from when a policy is created rather than GA, or an internal planning figure. Treat it as unverified.

Requirements & licensing

Area Requirement
Licence Intune Plan 1 + Windows licence with Autopatch entitlement (Windows Enterprise E3/E5 via microsoft-365-e3/microsoft-365-e5/F3, Education A3/A5, VDA E3/E5, M365 Business Premium)
Editions Pro, Pro Education, Enterprise, Education (not LTSC)
Join Intune-managed; microsoft-entra-id joined or hybrid joined
Data Diagnostic data ≥ Required; tenant consent for Intune to use it; wlidsvc running

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Gives predictable, compliant OS versions and an alternative to WSUS-style approvals.
  • The 36-month Enterprise window allows one major upgrade every 2–3 years, compared with a forced cadence on Pro (24 months). This is a concrete windows-11-enterprise differentiator. See windows-enterprise-servicing-lifecycle.

Limitations & gotchas

  • Pinning doesn't extend support, and a pinned Pro device loses support 12 months earlier than an Enterprise device on the same version.
  • Safeguard holds still apply, and policies take effect only after Autopilot OOBE.
  • Co-managed devices can briefly overshoot the target version when the workload moves to Intune. Create the policy first and wait for OfferReady.
  • If a device is removed from all policies under Autopatch, it gets no feature update until it is re-targeted.

[!warning] An older Intune page (2024) said core feature-update policy functions needed only an Intune licence, with Windows E3/E5 etc. required only for cloud extras like gradual rollout. The current 2026 page lists the Autopatch entitlement as a prerequisite. Check which applies before quoting to customers.

10-notes/entities/windows-hotpatch.title: Windows Hotpatch (Windows 11 Enterprise)
10-notes/entities/windows-hotpatch.html:
Windows Hotpatch (Windows 11 Enterprise)

What it is: Hotpatch delivers the monthly Patch Tuesday ("B") security update so that it installs and takes effect without a restart, in eight of twelve months. It is delivered through windows-autopatch quality update policies in microsoft-intune.

How it works

  • Baseline months (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct): a normal cumulative update (security + features + fixes) — restart required.
  • Hotpatch months (the other 8): security-only patch applied in memory — no restart.
  • Planned result: ~4 update restarts per year instead of 12.
  • Devices not on the current baseline get the baseline and the hotpatch (restart) in a hotpatch month.
  • Ineligible devices automatically fall back to the standard Latest Cumulative Update (LCU) — no gap in protection.
  • Packages are much smaller than LCUs → faster install, less bandwidth.
  • Enable in Intune: Devices › Windows updates › Quality updates › Windows quality update policy → "When available, apply without restarting the device (Hotpatch)" = Allow. Existing rings, deferrals, deadlines and active hours still apply.

Requirements & licensing

Area Requirement
Licence Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5, Microsoft 365 F3, Windows 11 Education A3/A5, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, or Windows 365 Enterprise
OS Windows 11 24H2 or later (not 26H1)
Security VBS turned on and running
Architecture x64 and Arm64; Arm64 must disable CHPE (HotPatchRestrictions=1 / DisableCHPE CSP + one restart)
Baseline Device on latest quarterly baseline
Management Intune + Windows Autopatch quality update policy, microsoft-entra-id joined/hybrid joined

Why it matters / customer talking points

  • Cuts forced patch restarts from 12 to ~4 a year → faster compliance with less user disruption.
  • Shrinks the "patched but not yet rebooted" window where a fix is downloaded but not active.
  • Good fit for frontline, clinical, trading floor and 24×7 devices. Strong add-on to the windows-11-enterprise / microsoft-365-e3 story alongside windows-expedited-updates.

Limitations & gotchas

  • VBS and baseline status are the most common reasons a device isn't eligible. Autopatch alerts flag "Hotpatch – VBS not running".
  • Arm64 + CHPE disabled can break 32-bit x86 apps (e.g., 32-bit Office VBA/COM add-ins). Exclude those devices or move apps to 64-bit.
  • No automatic rollback. You can uninstall a hotpatch, but that needs a restart.
  • Upgrading the feature version in a hotpatch month moves the device to standard LCUs (restart) until the next baseline. Upgrade in a baseline month instead.
  • Non-security (D-week) fixes and new features arrive only with baselines.

[!warning] The plan is 4 baselines a year, but Microsoft's 2026 calendar for 24H2/25H2 shows baselines in Jan, Apr, Jun, Jul, Sep and Oct — only Feb, Mar, May and Aug were hotpatch months. Present "4 restarts/year" as the planned cadence, not a guarantee.

[!question] Edition: the docs list licences, not OS editions. Business Premium is listed, but it does not include Windows Enterprise. That implies hotpatch works on Pro devices licensed through Business Premium. Learn does not state this explicitly, and its section heading says "Windows 11 Enterprise". Confirm before telling a Pro-only customer.

Summary — Copilot security readiness with Office 365 E1 Plus

Source: non-public field reference material reviewed 2026-10-19 (raw/2026-10-19-field-reference-material.ref.md); facts below are restated in general terms. Audience: ITDMs, IT security leads and CISOs.

Key takeaways

  1. Positioning: office-365-e1-plus is a low-cost first step toward zero-trust that gets a customer ready for microsoft-365-copilot. It is sold only in selected emerging markets as a promo SKU.
  2. Five controls frame Copilot security readiness: govern access (microsoft-entra-id P1, conditional-access); mitigate device risk (microsoft-intune P1); protect against threats (exchange-online-protection); protect against data loss (microsoft-purview DLP for email and files); discover AI apps (Cloud App Discovery, 400+ AI apps). See copilot-security-readiness.
  3. Good / better / best: E1 Plus = baseline, microsoft-365-e3 = "best-in-class" core and the jumping-off point, M365 E5 = automated and XDR-grade. See copilot-security-readiness.

Positioning outline

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot = LLM + Microsoft Graph + M365 apps, inside the compliance boundary.
  • Market context: leaders see AI as imperative but many lack a plan; data leakage is the main AI concern (see statistics below).
  • What E1 Plus contains, compared with O365 E1 and M365 E3.
  • Three value pillars: smart secure productivity (Copilot Chat with enterprise-data-protection), AI-era protection (Zero Trust), optimized IT management.
  • The five-step Copilot security journey (see takeaway 2).
  • Endpoint management: BYOD, consolidation, TCO.
  • E1 Plus vs M365 E3 vs M365 E5 control matrix.
  • Natural next step: M365 E3 + Copilot, starting with a solution assessment.

E1 Plus contents

OneDrive, Exchange, SharePoint, Viva Connections, Viva Engage, Viva Insights, Delve, Power Apps, Power Automate, Bookings, Stream, Sway, Forms, Planner, To Do, Entra ID P1, Office 365 DLP, Intune Plan 1.

  • Teams is a separate purchase for net-new customers; some Viva and Power Platform features depend on it.
  • Storage: 1 TB OneDrive and 50 GB mailbox for E1 and E1 Plus; 100 GB mailbox for M365 E3.

[!warning] Resolved: "Unlimited" for M365 E3 storage is out of date. Jaspreet confirmed 5 TB on 2026-10-19, which matches the E3 mind map (summary-m365-e3-feature-map#claim-002). Never quote "Unlimited".

The three E1 Plus differentiators over E1 are Intune P1, Office 365 DLP and Entra ID P1.

Staged Copilot rollout

  • Stage 1: web-grounded prompts. Microsoft Copilot in Bing, Edge and Windows with enterprise-data-protection.
  • Stage 2: Microsoft 365 Graph-grounded prompts. microsoft-365-copilot over the organization's data.
  • Build zero-trust protections while moving through the stages. See Microsoft Learn: Apply Zero Trust principles to Microsoft Copilots (learn.microsoft.com/security/zero-trust/copilots/apply-zero-trust-copilots-overview).

Identity detail

  • CAE triggers: user termination, password change or reset, network location change, token revocation. Policy is enforced without waiting for the token to expire.
  • Entra ID P1 in E1 Plus defends against password spray, replay and phishing.
  • Cloud App Discovery works by uploading network-device logs and reporting against a catalogue of 400+ gen-AI apps with compliance information.
  • Intune P1 covers Windows 11, macOS, iOS and Android.

Tier detail

  • E1 Plus ("baseline"): MFA, SSO, conditional-access, Cloud App Discovery, Intune P1, Purview DLP for email and files.
  • M365 E3 ("core"): + manual sensitivity and retention labels, including on non-Office files such as PDFs; discover gen-AI apps and alert on or block them on Windows 11 via microsoft-defender-for-endpoint P1; MDE P1 antimalware.
  • M365 E5 ("best-in-class"): + Entra ID Protection risk signals in Conditional Access; automatic sensitivity and retention labels; risk-adaptive controls, communication compliance and premium investigation; Defender for Cloud Apps to block or sanction 400+ AI apps; Defender XDR across endpoints, identity, cloud apps, email and files. See microsoft-365-e5.

Discovery questions

  • AI: What is your AI strategy for productivity? Have you identified the key roles to enable Copilot first, and how will you empower everyone else?
  • Security: What is your data protection strategy? Are your files in the cloud, on-premises or hybrid? Do you have a Zero Trust strategy, and how is it managed?
  • IT: How are endpoints managed today, and how is a new hire set up, remote or on-site? How many productivity and security vendors do you run, and have you considered consolidating?

Summary — Intune MDM and MAM for Microsoft 365 data protection

Source: Jaspreet's technical analysis, built from Microsoft Learn, Apple and vendor documentation (raw/2026-10-19-field-reference-material.ref.md); facts below are restated in general terms.

Key takeaways

  1. Enrolment is not enforcement. In M365, conditional-access reads a compliance state on the Entra ID device object. Only Intune, or an onboarded compliance partner (Jamf, Ivanti, SOTI, Omnissa, Scalefusion and others), can write it. manageengine is not onboarded, and its own documentation limits third-party MDM CA to enrolled Windows 10+ devices. So it gives no device-based CA on Android or iOS. See device-compliance-signal-flow.

  2. On BYOD, only the app layer enforces. The iOS enrolment type caps MDM restrictions, and Android Work Profile separates apps, not identities. Intune MAM provides:

    • conditional launch
    • app PIN
    • selective wipe
    • multi-identity
    • granular DLP
    • working with no enrolment at all

    See mdm-vs-mam.

  3. Commercial: Intune is already paid for in M365 E3, E5 and Business Premium. Since July 2026, E3 even includes Plan 2, Remote Help and Advanced Analytics. So a third-party UEM is a net-new cost plus a second console. Third-party "O365 DLP" modules (Scalefusion, 42Gears) still write Intune app protection policies through Graph and still need the Intune licence.

Other points

  • Defender containment loop:

    • Defender flags the device as high-risk.
    • Intune marks it non-compliant.
    • Entra updates the device object.
    • CA blocks access.

    This needs Intune-managed devices on Android and iOS, and Entra-joined or hybrid-joined devices on Windows. Without Intune there is no automatic consequence.

  • Windows-only stack: security baselines, ASR, BitLocker escrow, Windows LAPS, EPM, Autopilot and Autopatch.

  • Autopatch needs Windows Enterprise E3, E5 or F3.

  • Earlier licensing statement is out of date. Tunnel, Cloud PKI and EPM were described as Suite add-ons "not in E3 or E5". From July 2026, Tunnel is in E3 and Cloud PKI and EPM are in E5 (microsoft-intune-suite). This strengthens the argument, because the BYOD per-app VPN is now already licensed.

  • Counter-arguments addressed:

    • "enrol BYOD in ManageEngine"
    • "use IP-based CA" (IP is a location signal, not a trust signal)
    • "their console blocks copy-paste" (that is Intune APP through Graph)

  • Recommendation: consolidate on Intune, or run co-existence for specialist estates (rugged devices, Chrome OS, tvOS, Endpoint Central patching). Next step: an Intune BYOD pilot.

Contradictions with the vault

[!note] Resolved in the map's favour: Tunnel for MAM and Intune Plan 2 are in E3 from July 2026 (summary-m365-e3-feature-map#claim-003, summary-m365-e3-feature-map#claim-004).

[!note] Confirmed: Autopatch is available with F3, per Microsoft Learn (windows-autopatch#claim-002). The analysis was right.

Summary — Secure remote work for the public sector with Microsoft 365 E3

Source: Jaspreet's notes from a public-sector customer engagement (customer not named), see raw/2026-10-19-field-reference-material.ref.md; facts below are restated in general terms.

Key takeaways

  1. Positioning: a single microsoft-365-e3 licence per user delivers secure remote work across four pillars. The claim "no add-on licences required" needs the qualifications below:

    • identity and threat protection
    • devices and apps
    • collaboration
    • information protection

  2. Zero Trust mapping:

    • Verify explicitly: Entra ID P1 and WHfB
    • Least privilege: RBAC, labels, DLP
    • Assume breach: Defender for Office 365 P1, Intune compliance, Purview Audit and eDiscovery

    See zero-trust.

  3. Recommended path: a 1-day discovery workshop → a 4–6-week pilot (100 users, one department) → a Zero Trust baseline (CA, compliance, DLP for national ID, passport and tax data) → a staged rollout with Viva-led adoption.

Useful reusable content

  • Statistics (sources: Microsoft Digital Defense Report, IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2024, Verizon DBIR 2024; verify each figure against its report before reuse):
    • 99% of identity attacks are blocked by MFA
    • 22% of breaches start with stolen or weak credentials
    • $4.75M average public-sector breach cost
    • 73% of remote workers use unmanaged devices
    • 78% report remote-work security incidents
  • E3 contents: apps, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Viva (seeded), Entra ID P1, Intune, Defender for Office 365 P1, Windows 11 Enterprise, Purview (labels, DLP, retention, eDiscovery Core, Audit Standard with a 180-day log), Compliance Manager.

Contradictions with the vault

[!warning] Qualify identity claims. E3 includes Identity Protection only as limited visibility, and "just-in-time" only as time-limited access (Temporary Access Pass). Risk-based Conditional Access, automated remediation and PIM / JIT privileged role activation are E5 (Entra ID P2) only. See the table on microsoft-entra-id.

[!note] OneDrive: 1 TB is the default and 5 TB the maximum (confirmed by Jaspreet). Say "1 TB default, up to 5 TB".

[!warning] Defender Application Guard is deprecated. Do not list it (windows-11-enterprise#claim-002).

[!warning] Point-in-time restore is often mislabelled. It is not Windows Backup or File History. PITR restores the full system state from local VSS restore points captured in the last 72 hours, via WinRE. Frequency and retention are configurable on Enterprise only. See raw/2026-10-19-ms-learn-point-in-time-restore.ref.md.

[!warning] Labels are not automatic in E3. E3 (AIP / MIP Plan 1) gives manual labelling, and encryption follows once a user applies the label. Auto-labelling needs AIP Plan 2 / E5 (microsoft-purview).

Summary — Windows 11 Enterprise overview

Source: non-public field reference material reviewed 2026-10-19 (raw/2026-10-19-field-reference-material.ref.md); facts below are restated in general terms.

Key takeaways

  1. Three pillars: an AI-ready productivity platform (microsoft-365-copilot Chat, copilot-plus-pc); automated servicing (windows-autopatch, Hotpatch, org messages, remediations); and protection built for zero-trust (Credential Guard, windows-hello-for-business, TPM 2.0, Always-On VPN, BitLocker, PDE, universal-print).
  2. Windows Update for Business deployment service is merging into Autopatch. One dashboard in the Intune admin center, no feature loss, same licensing; Windows Autopatch comes with a Microsoft 365 E3 subscription.
  3. Forrester TEI study commissioned by Microsoft (2024; composite: 15,000 employees, 30,000 devices): +15% productive time from performance and +5% from UX; 10–15% fewer help-desk tickets; 60–80% less patching time (Autopatch); 20% lower printer spend (universal-print); 3% better risk profile.

Notable details

  • Copilot Chat with enterprise-data-protection: prompts and responses stay in the M365 service boundary and can be logged, retained and eDiscovered with Purview. They are not used for training. M365 Copilot lists at $30 per user per month.
  • Use rights: per-user subscription with up to 5 managed instances (Windows 11 Enterprise, Windows 365, AVD, VDA for VDI), 36 months of support per annual release, LTSC, and health, readiness and risk reports. See windows-virtualization-rights.
  • Support: Enterprise gets 36 months per feature update; Pro gets 24. See windows-enterprise-servicing.
  • Reports: Windows release health, the feature-update device-readiness report, the compatibility-risks report, and Microsoft Connected Cache.
  • App Assure: Microsoft's app-compatibility assistance programme.
  • DirectAccess is still supported, but moving to Always-On VPN is recommended.
  • Windows 10 end of support: 14 Oct 2025. Three paths: Windows 365 (includes ESU), upgrade eligible PCs, or buy new Pro PCs and step up with Autopilot.

[!note] Only the Always-On VPN device tunnel is an Enterprise feature. The user tunnel works on all editions (always-on-vpn).

agents.title: AGENTS — Vault Operating Manual
agents.html:
AGENTS.md

Operating manual for any AI agent (and for me) working in this Second Brain. Pattern: Karpathy-style LLM wiki — raw sources in, a compiled wiki out, governed by a schema.

1. Three layers and ownership

Layer Folders Owner Rule
Raw raw/, 00-Inbox/ Human Immutable. Agent may add a copy or reference; never edits or deletes.
Wiki 10-Notes/, 20-Projects/, 30-Areas/, 40-Resources/, index.md, log.md, _meta/MOCs/ Agent (human reviews) Compiled knowledge. Agent creates and updates; every claim traces to a raw source.
Schema AGENTS.md, _meta/conventions.md, _meta/templates/ Human Rules of the vault. Agent proposes changes; human approves.

2. Folder conventions and naming

Folder Holds
raw/ Original sources (PDFs, transcripts, clippings, links). Never modified.
00-Inbox/ Quick captures awaiting processing. Cleared weekly.
10-Notes/entities/ People, orgs, products, tools — one per page.
10-Notes/concepts/ Ideas, frameworks, patterns — one per page.
20-Projects/ Time-bound work with a goal and end date.
30-Areas/ Ongoing responsibilities (no end date).
40-Resources/ Source summaries and analysis pages.
50-Archive/ Finished or inactive items. Move, never delete.
_meta/ Schema, MOCs, templates.

Naming: atomic notes in kebab-case.md (e.g. microsoft-copilot.md); Inbox captures and raw files as YYYY-MM-DD-slug.ext; summaries as summary-<slug>.md; analyses as analysis-<slug>.md; MOCs as moc-<topic>.md (except home.md). Full rules: [[conventions]].

3. Page types and frontmatter

Types: entity, concept, summary, analysis, project, area, moc, capture, schema.

Every wiki page starts with:

---
title: Human-readable title
type: entity | concept | summary | analysis | project | area | moc | capture | schema
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
tags: [topic, subtopic]
sources: ["[[raw/2026-10-18-source-slug]]"]
status: draft | active | evergreen | stale | archived
---

A page missing any of the seven fields fails lint.

Optional: claims block

Use claims: in frontmatter for assertions worth tracking individually (facts, numbers, predictions, decisions). Most useful on entity, concept, summary and analysis pages.

claims:
  - id: claim-001
    text: "<one atomic assertion>"
    confidence: 0.8
    status: provisional | evergreen | disputed
    evidence:
      - source: raw/2026-10-19-source-slug.md
        kind: documentation | quote | observation
        excerpt: "<short quote, under 30 words>"
    captured: YYYY-MM-DD
    updated: YYYY-MM-DD

Rules:

  • id is unique within the page (claim-001, claim-002, …); cite elsewhere as [[page#claim-001]].
  • One assertion per claim. confidence is 0.0–1.0: below 0.5 is a hunch, 0.5–0.8 is likely, above 0.8 is well supported.
  • status: provisional = new or single-source; evergreen = confirmed by 2+ sources or durable by nature; disputed = credible evidence on both sides.
  • Every evidence.source points to a file in raw/, except an SME confirmation, which is written as source: "SME confirmation: <name>, <YYYY-MM-DD>" with kind: observation. documentation = official docs or specs; quote = a person's words; observation = something seen first-hand or confirmed by the SME.
  • When new evidence conflicts, add it to the claim, set status: disputed, adjust confidence, bump updated, and log it. Never delete evidence.

4. Operations

ingest (raw → wiki)

  1. Read the source in full.
  2. Save a copy or reference to raw/ as YYYY-MM-DD-slug.
  3. Give the human 1–3 key takeaways; discuss before writing.
  4. Write 40-Resources/summary-<slug>.md with citations.
  5. Create or update entity pages for people, orgs, products.
  6. Create or update concept pages for ideas worth tracking.
  7. Update relevant MOCs in _meta/MOCs/.
  8. Update index.md; append to log.md.
  9. Report every page touched.

query (wiki → answer)

  1. Read index.md first.
  2. Drill into relevant pages; follow [[links]].
  3. Synthesize an answer citing wiki pages; no fresh web search unless asked.
  4. If the answer is non-trivial, offer to file it as 40-Resources/analysis-<slug>.md, then update index and log.

lint (health check)

Report, then wait for approval before fixing.

Pages:

  • Contradictions — pages that disagree, in prose or in claims.
  • Orphans — pages nothing links to.
  • Stale pages — status: evergreen with page updated older than 90 days.
  • Missing — concepts mentioned often with no page; missing cross-references; missing frontmatter fields.
  • Inbox backlog — captures older than 7 days.

Claims:

  • Disputed — every claim with status: disputed, with its evidence on each side.
  • No evidence — claims with an empty evidence list, or a source that isn't in raw/.
  • Cross-page contradictions — two claims on different pages that assert incompatible things about the same subject.
  • Stale evergreen — status: evergreen claims with updated older than 90 days.
  • Confidence mismatch — evergreen claims below 0.8 confidence, or a single source with confidence above 0.8.

Report format: one table per check — page, claim id (if any), issue, suggested fix.

5. Log format

log.md is append-only, newest at the bottom, one line per event, greppable:

## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <subject>
- touched: [[page-a]], [[page-b]]
- note: one line on what changed or why

<op> is one of ingest, query, lint, fix, schema, archive, claim. Find all ingests: grep "] ingest" log.md.

6. House rules

  1. One idea per page. Split when a page covers two things.
  2. Cite sources. Every factual claim links to a raw/ file or a summary page; tracked claims carry evidence.
  3. Flag uncertainty. Mark unverified claims > [!question] and contradictions > [!warning].
  4. Link, don't duplicate. Reference an existing page instead of restating it.
  5. Never touch raw. Raw is append-only.
  6. Show before saving schema changes; wiki edits are reported after.
  7. Update updated: on every edit.
  8. Corrections go into the original page. When Jaspreet confirms, rules on or corrects something, edit the page(s) it affects: fix the text, add the confirmation as claim evidence (SME confirmation: Jaspreet Jolly, <date>), adjust the claim's status and confidence, and log it. Never create a standalone note for a ruling or confirmation, in raw/ or anywhere else.

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/vpn/vpn-connection-type — "VPN connection types" (Microsoft Learn), last updated date not shown
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing — "Windows Commercial Licensing overview", last updated 05/27/2026
  • https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows/docs/2026/06/directaccess-deprecation-on-future-windows-server-releases-a-new-era-of-always-on-connectivity — "DirectAccess deprecation on future Windows Server releases" (KB5103659), published June 11, 2026

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • User tunnel: supported on domain-joined, workgroup and Entra-joined devices and available in all Windows editions. Third parties can use the platform via UWP plug-ins. Protocols are SSTP and IKEv2.
  • Device tunnel: only on domain-joined Windows 10 Enterprise or Education 1709+. No third-party control. IKEv2 only with no SSTP fallback, machine-certificate auth, and split tunnel only (no force tunnel).
  • The Windows VPN technical guide's edition/licence tables show VPN = Yes on Pro, Enterprise, Pro Edu/SE and Education, and Yes for all licences including Pro.
  • The licensing overview lists "Always-On VPN device tunnel" among unique Enterprise features, but its Pro-vs-Enterprise table marks "Always On VPN" Yes/Yes (internal inconsistency).
  • AOVPN integrates with Windows Hello for Business, Entra Conditional Access (short-lived IPsec certs, 60 min default), NPS/RADIUS MFA, traffic and app filters, per-app VPN, trusted network detection and NRPT.
  • The connection flow uses an RRAS gateway as RADIUS client to NPS, which authorizes the connection.
  • Device tunnel traffic filters block inbound manage-out traffic. On RRAS, enable IKEv2 machine-cert auth and restrict it to an internal root CA.
  • DirectAccess is deprecated (KB5103659, June 2026) and will be removed from a future Windows Server. It's still in Server 2025. Microsoft recommends migrating to Always On VPN.

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/configure — "Configure BitLocker" (Microsoft Learn), last updated date not shown in fetched text

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing — "Windows Commercial Licensing overview", last updated 05/27/2026

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • BitLocker enablement: all editions (Pro, Enterprise, Pro Edu/SE, Education) and all licences, including Pro. The overview notes that enablement and management have different licensing requirements.
  • BitLocker management (Configure BitLocker page): supported on all four editions, but the licence entitlement is granted only by Enterprise E3/E5 and Education A3/A5. Pro licences don't grant it.
  • BitLocker CSP: added in Windows 10 1703 and supported on Pro since 1809. Every node shows ✅ Pro. A note says managing via CSP, other than enabling/disabling via RequireDeviceEncryption, needs Enterprise E3/E5 (also in M365 F3/E3/E5) or A3/A5 assigned to users, regardless of MDM platform.
  • The licensing overview lists "Modern BitLocker Management" as a Windows Enterprise feature but marks it Pro ✅ / Enterprise ✅ for edition, and says E3 capabilities "are not always technically enforced".
  • Default cipher is XTS-AES 128. The recommendation is XTS-AES, choosing 256-bit on faster hardware. A cipher change requires decrypting first. Startup PIN length is 4–20, with enhanced PINs optional.
  • Silent encryption: RequireDeviceEncryption=1 and AllowWarningForOtherDiskEncryption=0 (Entra-joined only), plus AllowStandardUserEncryption for standard users. It needs TPM, UEFI, Secure Boot and WinRE, and no startup PIN/key.
  • Recovery password rotation is via the ConfigureRecoveryPasswordRotation CSP or the Intune remote action (1909+/Win11), and needs "store recovery info before enabling" set to Required. Entra ID holds a maximum of 200 keys per device.
  • The Intune Encryption report shows encryption status and recovery keys. Key views are audited, and users can self-serve via Company Portal or My Account.
