raw/2026-10-19-credential-guardref.html:
Reference — Credential Guard (public sources)

URLs read

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/ — "Credential Guard overview" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 04/27/2026
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/remote-credential-guard — "Remote Credential Guard" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 03/29/2026
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing — "Windows Commercial Licensing overview" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 05/27/2026

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • Credential Guard uses VBS to isolate NTLM hashes, Kerberos TGTs and app-stored domain credentials so that even admin-level malware can't extract them. It blocks pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket attacks.
  • Edition table: Pro and Pro Education/SE = No; Enterprise and Education = Yes. Licence table: Windows Enterprise E3/E5 and Education A3/A5 grant it; Pro licences don't.
  • Default-on from Windows 11 22H2 (and Server 2025 domain-joined non-DCs) when licence and hardware requirements are met and it isn't explicitly disabled. Enabled without UEFI lock, so it can be turned off remotely. A pre-existing explicit disable survives the upgrade.
  • Requirements: VBS and Secure Boot. Recommended: TPM 1.2/2.0 and UEFI lock. Hyper-V Gen 2 VMs only, and the host needs an IOMMU.
  • Breaks Kerberos DES, unconstrained delegation, TGT extraction and NTLMv1. Digest, CredSSP, credential delegation and MS-CHAPv2 prompt for credentials and expose them to risk.
  • Not recommended on DCs and not supported on Exchange Server. Doesn't protect the AD database or SAM.
  • Remote Credential Guard: redirects Kerberos for RDP so credentials never go to the target host. It is supported on Pro, Enterprise and Education with all licences. It's Kerberos-only, needs AD-joined targets, isn't supported via RD Gateway/Broker, and Restricted Admin is recommended for helpdesk use.
  • The licensing overview lists Credential Guard as Enterprise-only (Pro ❌).

raw/2026-10-19-ms-learn-point-in-time-re.title: Reference — Microsoft Learn: Point-in-time restore for Windows
raw/2026-10-19-ms-learn-point-in-time-re.html:
Reference — Microsoft Learn: Point-in-time restore for Windows

URL: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/point-in-time-restore (applies to Windows 11; last updated 10/15/2026). Read on 2026-10-19. Summary in my own words.

  • What it does: restores a Windows 11 PC to its full earlier state (OS, apps, settings, local files) in minutes, using local VSS restore points from the last 72 hours.
  • Capture: automatic. Default about every 24 hours; configurable to 4, 6, 12, 16 or 24 hours.
  • Retention: default 72 hours; configurable down to 4 hours.
  • Space cap: default 2% of disk, between 2 GB and 50 GB. Restore points are evicted first when free space drops to 20 GB or less.
  • Edition split:
    • On/off and the space cap: Home, Pro and Enterprise.
    • Frequency and retention: Enterprise only.
    • On by default: unmanaged Home and Pro (OS volume of 200 GB or more).
    • Off by default: Enterprise and Education, and managed or domain-joined Pro.
  • Management: Recovery CSP PointInTimeRestore node (enable, max disk usage, frequency, retention), or Settings > System > Recovery.
  • Restore: local only, from WinRE (Troubleshoot > Point-in-time restore). Needs the BitLocker recovery key. Changes after the restore point are lost, but OneDrive cloud data is unaffected. It can roll back recent security updates or policies, so validate afterwards. Only the OS volume is restored. EFS-encrypted files block restore.
  • Versus System Restore: PITR is scheduled-only, covers the full system, keeps restore points 72 hours at most, uses reserved storage and supports remote management. System Restore is event-triggered or manual and covers system files and settings only.
  • Versus Windows 365 PITR: the Cloud PC version keeps restore points up to a month in cloud storage.

Reference — Personal Data Encryption (public sources)

URLs read

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/personal-data-encryption/ — "Personal Data Encryption overview" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 03/13/2025
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/personal-data-encryption/configure — "Personal Data Encryption settings and configuration" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 03/13/2025
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing — "Windows Commercial Licensing overview" (Microsoft Learn), last updated 05/27/2026
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/protect/encrypt-devices (resolved to .../intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/encrypt-bitlocker-windows) — "Encrypt Windows devices with BitLocker using Intune", last updated 04/15/2026

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • PDE is file-based encryption whose keys are bound to Windows Hello for Business. Keys are released at Hello sign-in and discarded at sign-out. It uses AES-CBC 256.
  • Known-folder PDE (Desktop, Documents, Pictures) requires Windows 11 24H2+. Base PDE requires 22H2+.
  • Prerequisites: Entra joined or hybrid joined (domain-joined-only isn't supported), Windows Hello sign-in and ARSO disabled. Password or FIDO2 sign-in can't open protected content. If the prerequisites aren't met, Windows falls back to DPAPI.
  • Editions: Enterprise and Education only. Licences: Enterprise E3/E5 and Education A3/A5. The licensing overview also marks PDE as Pro ❌.
  • Level 1 vs Level 2: Level 2 discards keys one minute after lock. Neither level allows access via UNC or RDP.
  • PDE complements BitLocker and doesn't replace it. Microsoft recommends using both, plus OneDrive backup and the WHfB PIN reset service, because a destructive PIN reset or TPM reset loses the keys.
  • Hardening: disable hibernation, crash/live dumps and WER, plus the connected-standby password-delay policy. PDE is off by default. Configure it via Intune Disk encryption → PDE profile, the settings catalog or the PDE CSP.
  • Disabling PDE auto-decrypts known-folder content but not API-protected files (use cipher /d).

raw/2026-10-19-point-in-time-restoreref.html:
Reference — Point-in-time restore (public sources)

URLs read

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/point-in-time-restore — "Point-in-time restore for Windows | Microsoft Learn" — last updated 2026-10-15
  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/recovery-csp — "Recovery CSP | Microsoft Learn" — last updated 2026-09-23

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • Full-system VSS snapshots stored locally (OS, apps, settings, local files); restore covers roughly the previous 72 hours; default capture about every 24 h.
  • Frequency (4/6/12/16/24 h) and retention (4–72 h) are Enterprise-only settings; on/off and max usage (default 2% of disk, 2–50 GB) are available on Home, Pro, Enterprise.
  • On by default for Home and unmanaged Pro when the OS volume is ≥200 GB; off by default for Enterprise, Education and managed/domain-joined Pro.
  • Restore is started only from WinRE (described as preview); BitLocker recovery key required; user acknowledges data-loss risk.
  • Points are pruned when >72 h old, when VSS max is reached, or free space ≤20 GB; VSS failures can remove all points; space shared with other VSS tools.
  • Cloud data such as OneDrive is unaffected; local changes after the point, recent updates and policies may be rolled back — validate after restore.
  • Limitations: OS volume only, no export/mount, not across edition changes, EFS files block restore; known issues with Outlook .ost, Recall, BitLocker auto-unlock.
  • Differs from System Restore (manual/event-triggered, indefinite, partial scope) and from Windows 365 Enterprise PITR (always on, up to one month, short/long-term/manual points, cloud storage).
  • Recovery CSP PointInTimeRestore node applies to Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise on Windows 11 24H2 26100.8737 / 25H2 26200.8737 and later.

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • QMR builds on Startup Repair: after repeated boot failures, WinRE connects to the network and checks Windows Update for a remediation, applies it and restarts; it's best-effort.
  • Two controls: cloud remediation (use Windows Update vs. local Startup Repair only) and auto remediation (automatic scan, once or on a retry loop, vs. manual).
  • Defaults: on (one-time scan) for Home and unmanaged Pro; off for Enterprise, Education, domain-joined/managed Pro and Windows Server 2025. Admin-set values persist across management-state changes.
  • Only wired and WPA/WPA2 password Wi-Fi supported in WinRE; CSP can reuse saved Wi-Fi profiles.
  • Config: Recovery CSP QuickMachineRecovery node (EnableQuickMachineRecovery, EnableAutoRemediation, SetRetryInterval 0–4320, SetTimeToReboot 1–4320 / max 72 h) applicable from Windows 11 24H2 26100.8737 and 25H2 26200.8737; reagentc XML; Settings; GPO only for Server 2025.
  • Test mode (reagentc /SetRecoveryTestmode then /BootToRe) is limited to Insider Experimental channel.
  • WRI blog (June 2025): QMR announced for all Windows 11 24H2 editions, on by default for Home, admin-controlled for Pro/Enterprise; part of WRI alongside Connected Cache, Universal Print anywhere, hotpatch and Windows 365 Reserve.
  • Learn page meta description references a "RemoteRemediation CSP" while the body points to the Recovery CSP (naming inconsistency).

Verified facts

  • Universal Print entitlement is bundled in commercial, education and government Microsoft 365 and Windows Enterprise subscriptions, and is also sold standalone. — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/universal-print/get-access-to-universal-print (last updated 2025-07-21)

  • Over-use doesn't stop printing; the admin is alerted and is expected to buy add-ons/licences to stay compliant. — same URL

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • One update per policy, chosen by release date. Non-security D/OOB updates can be expedited on Windows 11 only.
  • The restart deadline is configurable at 0, 1 or 2 days. After the deadline the device restarts even during active hours, and a manual restart cancels the scheduled forced restart.
  • Licensing: Intune Plan 1 plus a Windows licence that carries the Autopatch entitlement. Autopatch prerequisites list Business Premium, Education A3/A5, Enterprise E3/E5 (incl. M365 F3/E3/E5) and E3/E5 VDA.
  • Supported editions are Pro, Pro Education, Enterprise and Education; LTSC is not supported. Devices must be Entra joined or hybrid joined and Intune-managed, with telemetry at Required or higher and wlidsvc running.
  • Update Health Tools are needed before 24H2 and must be removed on 24H2+.
  • Reports live in Reports › Windows Updates (summary + expedited report) and Devices › Monitor (policies with alerts). Device states run Pending/Offering/Installing/Installed.
  • Settings that can block expedite: WSUS server URL, AutoUpdateCfg, DeferFeatureUpdates, Disable Dual Scan, pre-release builds, and notifications turned off.

  • Windows Autopatch prerequisites — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-autopatch/prepare/windows-autopatch-prerequisites — last updated 2026-02-26
  • (Search snippet only, not fetched) older Intune page "Feature updates for Windows 10 and later policy" (learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/mem/intune/protect/windows-10-feature-updates, dated 2024-09-10). It said core functions need only an Intune licence.
  • (Search) query for "1,060 days" Windows feature update: no Microsoft source found.

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • A feature update policy pins devices to one target version, upgrades devices below it, never downgrades, and persists until changed. A ring pause lasts only 35 days.
  • Only in-support versions can be selected. Intune shows a Support End Date (Enterprise/Education), a "Support Ending" status inside 2 months, and "Not supported" after that, at which point the version no longer deploys.
  • Current prerequisites: Intune Plan 1 plus a Windows licence with the Autopatch entitlement. Supported editions are Pro, Pro Edu, Enterprise and Edu; LTSC is not supported. Telemetry must be at Required or higher.
  • Servicing lengths are 36 months for Enterprise/Education and 24 months for Pro/Home. 24H2 Enterprise support ends 2027-10-12 and 25H2 ends 2028-10-10.
  • The device readiness report rates each device Low/Medium/High risk or Replace device, and the compatibility risks report lists top app/driver risks. Both are based on diagnostic data with up to ~52 h latency. Autopatch prerequisites list device readiness for Business Premium, A3+, E3+ and F3.
  • Set the ring feature-update deferral to 0 when using policies. When multiple policies apply, the latest version wins.
  • No public source documents a "1,060 days" pin limit.

Reference — Windows Hotpatch (public sources)

URLs read

  • Hotpatch updates (Windows Autopatch) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-autopatch/manage/windows-autopatch-hotpatch-updates — last updated 2026-06-01
  • Windows 11 release information (incl. hotpatch calendar) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-health/windows11-release-information — last updated 2026-10-13
  • Manage Windows quality updates (Intune) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/windows/manage-quality-updates — last updated 2026-04-09
  • Windows Autopatch prerequisites — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-autopatch/prepare/windows-autopatch-prerequisites — last updated 2026-02-26

Key facts (paraphrased)

  • Hotpatch applies the monthly B security release without a restart. It is configured through an Intune/Autopatch Windows quality update policy (hotpatch setting = Allow).
  • Eligible licences: Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5, Microsoft 365 F3, Windows 11 Education A3/A5, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, and Windows 365 Enterprise.
  • Requires Windows 11 24H2+ and VBS running, and the device must be on the latest baseline. Arm64 devices must disable CHPE (registry HotPatchRestrictions=1 or DisableCHPE CSP).
  • Planned cadence: baseline (restart) in Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, hotpatch in the other eight months. Extra baselines can be added for security reasons without moving the planned ones.
  • In the 2026 calendar for 24H2/25H2, June and September were also baselines, so 2026 had only four hotpatch months: Feb, Mar, May and Aug.
  • Ineligible devices get the normal LCU. Rollback isn't automatic, and uninstalling a hotpatch needs a restart.
  • If you do a feature upgrade during a hotpatch month, the device switches to standard updates until the next baseline. Hotpatch is not available on 26H1.
  • Hotpatch packages are much smaller than LCUs. Existing rings, deferrals, deadlines and active hours still apply.

Addendum — Windows Enterprise use rights

Verified facts

  • Windows 11 Enterprise E3 and E5 are per-user subscriptions sold only via commercial licensing (incl. CSP) and require Windows Pro as the qualifying OS. — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing (last updated 2026-05-27)
  • The overview lists "five Windows instances per licensed user" as an Enterprise use right, illustrated as a laptop plus a Cloud PC plus a specialized LTSC device, etc. — same URL
  • Listed included rights also cover Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365 Enterprise and VDA access rights (with FSLogix), 36-month support for annual feature releases, Windows LTSC Enterprise, MDOP, and release-health/readiness reports. — same URL
  • Windows Enterprise E3 delivered through Microsoft 365 F3 excludes MDOP, Windows LTSC Enterprise and Windows Autopatch. — same URL
  • E5 adds Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 on top of E3. — same URL
  • Product Terms: users with Entra ID-based activation may activate Windows in the physical OS on up to five concurrent devices. — https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/productoffering/WindowsDesktopOperatingSystem/EAEAS
  • Product Terms: per-user licensing requires the licensed user to be primary user of at least one primary work device licensed with a qualifying OS. — same URL
  • Product Terms: users with M365 E3/E5/F3/Business Premium/A3/A5, Windows Enterprise E3/E5, Education A3/A5 or VDA E3/E5 may access AVD Windows VMs, and AVD VMs don't count toward the activation device limit. — same URL
  • Product Terms (SA/subscription rights): up to four local virtual OSEs per licensed device/user, and remote access to up to four virtual OSEs or one physical OSE. — same URL
  • Product Terms: Windows Enterprise per-user users may run Windows 11 VMs in their own Azure accounts, accessing up to four instances. — same URL
  • Windows VDA (per device or per user) licenses access to virtual desktops from devices without qualifying Enterprise/VDA rights, e.g., thin clients. — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/windows-licensing

_meta/conventions.title: Vault Conventions
_meta/conventions.html:
Conventions

File naming

  • Atomic notes (entities, concepts): kebab-case.md — azure-openai.md, second-brain.md.
  • Inbox captures and raw files: YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md — 2026-10-18-copilot-roadmap.md.
  • Summaries: summary-<slug>.md. Analyses: analysis-<slug>.md.
  • Lowercase, hyphens only, no spaces or special characters, no dates in atomic note names.

Frontmatter

Required on every page: title, type, created, updated, tags, sources, status.

---
title: Azure OpenAI
type: entity
created: 2026-10-18
updated: 2026-10-18
tags: [ai, microsoft, product]
sources: ["[[summary-azure-openai-overview]]"]
status: active
---

---
title: 2026-10-18 Copilot roadmap note
type: capture
created: 2026-10-18
updated: 2026-10-18
tags: [inbox]
sources: []
status: draft
---

Status values: draft → active → evergreen; stale, archived as needed.

Links

  • Use [[wiki-links]] by filename, no extension: [[azure-openai]].
  • Alias with a pipe: [[azure-openai|AOAI]].
  • Link to a heading: [[second-brain#Layers]].
  • Every new page links to at least one existing page and one MOC.

Tags

  • Lowercase, kebab-case, plural-free: #ai, #customer, #modern-work.
  • Max 5 tags per page.
  • Hierarchy with /: #customer/acme, #area/sci.
  • Tags group; links relate. Don't use a tag where a link fits.

MOCs

  • Live in _meta/MOCs/.
  • Name: moc-<topic>.md; landing page is home.md.
  • Create a MOC when a topic has 5+ notes.
  • home.md links to every MOC.

Weekly Inbox processing (every Friday)

  • Open 00-Inbox/; handle oldest first.
  • For each capture: delete, promote to a note, or ingest as a source.
  • Move source material to raw/.
  • Add frontmatter and links to anything promoted.
  • Update relevant MOCs and index.md.
  • Append one log.md entry for the session.
  • Inbox is empty, or every leftover item has a reason.
